title: PRD Draft (WIP): Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds + Predictive Mode
content:
Doc status: early PRD draft. Expect gaps + open questions. This will be converted into the Confluence PRD once we lock semantics + GA criteria.

Author: Lauren Bishop (Product, Dedicated)
Program: Talia Benson
Last updated: 2025-06-27

1) Summary / TL;DR
Enterprise Dedicated customers want contractual/operational guardrails on scaling behavior.
- Bounds: customer sets hard min/max capacity per Dedicated deployment (replicas and/or GPUs), enforced deterministically.
- Predictive mode (optional): bias scale decisions using forecasted demand (time-of-day ramps, scheduled events, historical patterns) to avoid cold-start and queue buildup.
- Safety: avoid oscillation, avoid unsafe scale-down, preserve isolation, and never exceed max or drop below min.
- Operability: dashboards, alerts, auditability (who/what/when) for config changes and scaling decisions.

2) Problem statement
Today Dedicated scaling is mostly platform-driven based on reactive signals (saturation, queue depth, latency) with occasional operator overrides. Customers (esp. enterprise) report two recurring issues:
A) Spend unpredictability during bursts: they want a hard ceiling to prevent unplanned scale-up (budget caps / procurement constraints).
B) Predictable ramps still cause latency/queue spikes: reactive scaling triggers too late, and cold start / provisioning delay shows up in p95/p99.

Supporting signals (recent)
- SUP-28411: customer asks for hard max bound to prevent unexpected scale-up.
- SUP-28437: daily ramp causes queueing; wants pre-scale (predictive) without manual playbooks.
- HubSpot notes (Northstar Fintech / Hexagon Support Systems): both called out cost ceilings + baseline capacity as blockers/close drivers.

Customer quote snippets (paraphrased from discovery notes / calls)
- “We can’t wake up to a 3x bill because an upstream system misbehaved.”
- “Traffic ramp is always 8:45–9:15am local; if you’re only reacting once queues form, we already lost the SLA.”

3) Goals
G1. Customer-configurable bounds
- Provide per-deployment min and max capacity bounds for Dedicated deployments.
- Bounds must take precedence over platform defaults.
- Deterministic enforcement + observability (requested desired vs bounded desired).

G2. Predictive scaling mode (opt-in)
- Add an option to incorporate forecast signal(s) to pre-scale ahead of demand.
- Must gracefully fall back to reactive-only when forecasts are stale/unavailable.
- Must always respect bounds.

G3. Safety + reliability
- Avoid oscillation and flapping (cooldowns/dampening).
- Avoid scale-down below safe baseline; never violate min.
- Clear behavior under conflicting signals (predictive vs reactive).

G4. Operability + auditability
- Audit log config changes (who/when/what) and autoscaler decisions (inputs + reasoning summary).
- Dashboards and alerts for: bound-hit rate, queue depth, unmet min (capacity shortage), prediction error.
- Runbooks + clear escalation paths.

G5. Customer experience
- Expose in Console and API (and eventually Terraform).
- Documentation: semantics, recommended ranges, and how to choose bounds.
- CS enablement: playbooks + “how to interpret bounded scaling metrics” for QBRs and escalations.

4) Non-goals (for initial release)
- Cross-region active-active predictive placement optimization.
- Fully automated procurement workflows triggered by predictions.
- Dynamic contract renegotiation flows.

5) Personas / users
P1. Platform engineer at an enterprise customer (Dedicated)
- Needs predictable baseline throughput and hard budget ceilings.
- Wants to set min to ensure baseline SLOs, set max for spend control.

P2. SRE / on-call at customer
- Needs to understand “why are we queuing?” quickly.
- Needs deterministic logs/metrics to correlate scaling actions and latency.

P3. Redwood SRE / support
- Needs to triage “we’re stuck at max” and “min isn’t met” and have safe mitigations.

6) Proposed solution / product behavior (draft semantics)
6.1 Scaling bounds (hard enforcement)
- min_replicas: lower bound. Autoscaler cannot go below.
- max_replicas: upper bound. Autoscaler cannot exceed.
- If only max is set: current baseline behavior remains, but scale-up is clamped.
- If only min is set: ensures baseline, but can still scale up per normal logic.

Important: “Hard” means the control loop clamps desired capacity; it does not just warn.

6.2 Relationship to platform defaults
Draft proposal:
- Platform retains default policy (reactive signals, target utilization, etc.) to compute requested_desired.
- Bounds layer clamps to bounded_desired = clamp(requested_desired, min, max).
- Autoscaler acts on bounded_desired.
- Emit both numbers and a reason in structured logs and metrics.

6.3 Predictive mode (opt-in)
Draft proposal:
- Add a “predictive_mode” setting per deployment:
  - off (default)
  - on (use prediction to bias requested_desired)
- Predictive mode produces predicted_desired (or predicted_load converted to replicas) and merges with reactive requested_desired.
- Reactive signals (saturation/queue) can override prediction when prediction is wrong (i.e., ensure scale-up happens even if forecast underestimates), but still respect max.
- If forecast is missing/stale/untrusted: fallback to reactive-only.

Key details to be decided (open questions below):
- Merge policy: max(reactive, predictive) vs weighted blend vs stepwise.
- How to set “lead time” and “confidence”.

6.4 Cooldowns / anti-oscillation
- Add scale-up and scale-down cooldowns.
- Add dampening/step-size constraints to avoid flapping when predicted demand jittery.
- Add minimum time above/below threshold before scaling down.

6.5 Capacity shortages and “unmet min”
- If min cannot be provisioned due to region capacity shortage, the system should:
  - keep retrying with backoff
  - surface degraded state clearly (Console + metrics)
  - trigger alerting to Redwood SRE
  - provide CS-facing comms guidance

7) Requirements (draft)
7.1 Functional requirements
R1. Control plane schema for scaling policy
- Fields (draft):
  - enabled (bool) OR presence implies enabled
  - min_replicas (int >= 0)
  - max_replicas (int >= 0)
  - scale_up_cooldown_seconds
  - scale_down_cooldown_seconds
  - predictive_mode (enum: off/on)
  - predictive_timezone (optional) / schedule alignment (TBD)
  - prediction_staleness_seconds (TBD default)
- Validation:
  - if both set, min <= max
  - prevent absurd values (guardrails by SKU/contract?)
  - RBAC: only specific roles can change bounds
  - rate-limit repeated config updates to prevent churn (customer or buggy automation)

R2. Autoscaler enforcement
- Clamp desired to bounds.
- Emit:
  - requested_desired
  - bounded_desired
  - clamp_reason (min_clamp / max_clamp / none)
  - signal_inputs summary (queue depth, util, prediction age)

R3. Predictive signal integration
- Define forecast interface (inputs/outputs) and staleness rules.
- Ensure safe behavior if predictor returns null/NaN.
- Ensure predictable ramp leads to pre-scale within lead time.

R4. Console UI
- Per deployment settings page includes bounds and predictive toggle.
- Display “effective policy” and a preview of implications (best-effort).
- Validation error states: min>max, too high min vs purchased capacity, cooldown too low.

R5. Observability
- Metrics + dashboard panels:
  - desired_requested vs desired_bounded
  - bound_hit_rate (max bound clamp frequency)
  - queue depth, saturation, latency correlation
  - prediction vs actual demand, prediction error
  - unmet_min indicator during shortage

R6. Audit logging
- Log policy changes (who/when/what).
- Log scaling decisions with reasoning and inputs.
- Retention suitable for enterprise compliance (TBD exact days by tier).

7.2 Reliability / safety requirements
- Invariants:
  - never exceed max
  - never go below min
  - no scale-to-zero surprises (unless explicitly allowed; default disallow for Dedicated)
- Deterministic evaluation order and recorded reasoning.
- Backward compatible defaults: existing deployments should see no behavior change until explicitly enabled.

7.3 Supportability requirements
- CS playbook: common misconfigs, how to pick min/max, what to do when max hit.
- SRE runbook: stuck scale, prediction pipeline outage, unmet min, how to temporarily disable predictive mode.

8) UX / API sketch (very rough)
Console: Dedicated Deployment → “Scaling” tab
- Autoscaling: [On]
- Min replicas: [ 4 ] (helper text: baseline capacity)
- Max replicas: [ 20 ] (helper text: cost ceiling)
- Predictive scaling: [Off/On]
  - When On: show “Forecast status” (healthy/stale/unavailable) + last updated timestamp
- Advanced: cooldowns
- Audit: “Recent scaling decisions” link

API sketch (names TBD):
PATCH /v1/dedicated/deployments/{deployment_id}/scaling_policy
{
  min_replicas: 4,
  max_replicas: 20,
  predictive_mode: "on",
  scale_up_cooldown_seconds: 120,
  scale_down_cooldown_seconds: 300
}

9) Success metrics (draft)
Customer outcomes
- Reduced incidents of “unexpected spend” / “exceeded budget cap” (proxy: support tickets, churn risk notes).
- Improved latency during predictable ramps:
  - p95 latency during ramp window improves by X% vs reactive-only baseline (target TBD by pilot results)
  - reduced queue depth spikes and time spent in saturation

Platform outcomes
- Bound-hit observability: in pilots, we can attribute bound-hit events to known caps, not bugs.
- Prediction error tracked and does not increase incident rate.
- No regressions in autoscaler stability (oscillation rate below threshold).

Adoption
- % of eligible Dedicated deployments enabling bounds within 60 days of GA (target TBD).
- # of enterprise accounts using predictive mode (likely smaller; only when confidence is high).

10) Rollout plan (draft)
Phase 0: Discovery + semantics lock
- align with Eng/SRE on invariants and precedence (ADR)

Phase 1: Build control plane + enforcement (bounds only)
- ship behind feature flag per account/deployment

Phase 2: Predictive mode pilot
- integrate forecast interface + staleness/fallback
- pilot with 1–3 customers with known ramps

Phase 3: Canary by region
- start with one region (likely us-east) and a narrow cohort
- SRE readiness review + game day

Phase 4: GA
- docs, Console UX polish, support enablement, Terraform follow-up if feasible

11) Dependencies / cross-team
- Platform control plane (schema, RBAC, validation): Ethan Park / Benji Okafor / Jordan Lee
- Fleet autoscaler: Vanessa Ortiz / Keiko Yamamoto
- Observability dashboards/alerts: Allison Grant / Sergio Costa
- SRE readiness + runbooks: Rafael Mendes / Miles Thornton
- Routing integration (bounded capacity state): Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon
- Compliance/audit: Naomi Feldman / Marcus Lin

12) Risks / concerns
- Customer sets min too high → capacity planning + shortage risk; needs guardrails and clear messaging.
- Predictive mode incorrect forecasts → overshoot (cost) or undershoot (queueing). Must have fallback to reactive scale-up and dampening.
- High-cardinality metrics if we label too granularly (deployment_id + customer_id + model + etc.). Need careful metric naming/labels.
- Confusion about “hard” vs “recommended”. UI needs to communicate that bounds are enforced.
- Contract alignment: if bounds are “contractual”, do we need enforcement even under overload? (e.g., can we temporarily exceed max for safety?) Current stance: never exceed max; handle via graceful degradation and customer comms.

13) Open questions (to resolve before Confluence PRD)
Semantics / precedence
Q1. Should bounds be strictly enforced even during overload/incident? (Current proposal: yes; never exceed max.)
Q2. What is the precedence between predictive vs reactive?
- Option A: requested_desired = max(reactive_desired, predictive_desired)
- Option B: predictive sets a floor for scale-up only (pre-scale), reactive still drives scale-down
- Option C: blend based on confidence

Q3. Do we support bounds in GPUs vs replicas, or both?
- Dedicated capacity is often thought of as “GPUs”. But autoscaler controls replicas. Do we need a translation layer that accounts for model per-replica GPU allocation?

Q4. Do we allow min=0 for Dedicated?
- My leaning: disallow by default; maybe allow for dev/test tiers explicitly.

Q5. How should “unmet min” be represented to customers?
- UI badge + alert? Does the customer get notified automatically?

Config + validation
Q6. What is the recommended min/max guidance?
- Should we show a “platform recommended range” and allow override?
- Should we enforce upper limits based on purchased commit or account quotas?

Q7. Rate limits on config changes
- How strict? Example: no more than N updates per hour per deployment.

Predictive mode
Q8. What inputs are available for forecasting in v1?
- time-of-day patterns, historical request rate, queue depth history, customer scheduled events.

Q9. Forecast SLA and failure modes
- If predictor is down or stale, do we just ignore it (fallback)? How to surface that predictive is inactive?

Q10. Timezone / scheduled events
- Customers talk in local time. Do we store timezone in policy? Or do we keep everything in UTC and require customer to adapt?

Observability / compliance
Q11. Audit log retention by tier
- What do we promise for Dedicated enterprise? 30/90/365 days?

Q12. Metric labels and cardinality
- Which labels are mandatory (customer_id, deployment_id, region) vs too expensive?

14) Pilot candidate notes (draft)
- Northstar Fintech: strict max cap + baseline min; willing to pilot; cares about procurement optics.
- Hexagon Support Systems: daily ramp; wants predictive; had security/compliance requirements (audit logs).
- Polaris Analytics: POC success criteria includes max bound enforcement + p95 during ramp.

15) Work-in-progress notes / iteration history
- 2025-06-10: Created doc after Dedicated customer discovery round (cost cap + ramp issues).
- 2025-06-14: Added explicit invariants and first pass on API/Console concepts (after sync with Ethan/Vanessa).
- 2025-06-20: Added predictive mode section and open questions after internal review with SRE (Rafael) re: safety/oscillation.
- 2025-06-27: Expanded observability + audit requirements; linked initial tickets (PM-1842, ENG-22140..22143) and support inputs (SUP-28411, SUP-28437).

16) Next steps
- Align on semantics with Eng/SRE; draft ADR (bounds precedence + safety invariants).
- Define v1 schema fields and validation rules; confirm RBAC.
- Identify pilot cohort and success criteria; finalize rollout gating.
- Convert this draft into Confluence PRD + design spec once Q1–Q12 are resolved.

Appendix: References (internal)
- Linear epic: PM-1842 Autoscaling bounds + predictive mode
